was heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One)
<s>Arhats</s> (worthy ones), with outflows destroyed, free from afflictions, self-mastered,
wisdom, thoroughbreds, great <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-kings), who had done what was to be done,

And from that tongue-faculty, many hundreds of thousands of millions of rays of various colors issued forth. Then, in that instant, moment, and second, whatever hells, animal realms, <s>Yama</s>-worlds, states of woe, bad destinies, and downfalls existed in this triple-thousand great-thousand world-system — they were all completely cut off. children.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practicing in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not connect the eye-element (<s>cakṣurdhātu</s>) with emptiness, nor emptiness with the eye-element; does not connect the form-element (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) with emptiness, nor emptiness with the form-element; does not connect the eye-consciousness-element (<s>cakṣurvijñānadhātu</s>) with emptiness, nor emptiness with the eye-consciousness-element. Similarly, [he does not connect with emptiness] the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element, the nose-element, the smell-element, the nose-consciousness-element, the tongue-element, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element, the body-element, the tangible-element, the body-consciousness-element; up to: he does not connect the mind-element (<s>manodhātu</s>) with emptiness, nor emptiness with the mind-element; does not connect the dharma-element with emptiness, nor emptiness with the dharma-element; does not connect the mind-consciousness-element (<s>manovijñānadhātu</s>) with emptiness, nor emptiness with the mind-consciousness-element. This indeed, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is the supreme <s>yoga</s> (practice), namely the <s>yoga</s> of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā-yoga</s>). Practicing the <s>yoga</s> of emptiness, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not fall into the stage of <s>Śrāvakas</s> or the stage of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; he purifies the <s>Buddha</s>-field, matures beings, and quickly awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Whatever <s>yogas</s> there may be, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>yoga</s> of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is declared supreme among them, the best, the most excellent, the foremost, the most refined. For what reason? This <s>yoga</s> is unsurpassed, namely the <s>yoga</s> of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>yoga</s> of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (<s>śūnyatā-ānimitta-apraṇihita-yoga</s>). children.translated_text: For he does not differentiate from the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, nor does he perceive any <s>dharma</s> other than the <s>dharmadhātu</s>—[be it one] who would practice in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, or who would be predicted by <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, or who would awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening. For what reason? For that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, practicing in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not give rise to the perception of a being (<s>satva-saṃjñā</s>), nor the perception of a living being (<s>jīva-saṃjñā</s>), nor the perception of a person (<s>pudgala-saṃjñā</s>), nor the perception of a knower, seer, doer, or experiencer. // For what reason? For ultimately a being is not found and does not cease. For there is neither arising nor cessation of a being, and of that which has neither arising nor cessation, how shall it practice in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? Thus practicing, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> through the non-arising of beings, through the emptiness of beings, through the non-apprehension of beings, through the seclusion of beings, through the nature of beings, through the non-own-nature of beings. This, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is the supreme <s>yoga</s> of <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, namely the <s>yoga</s> of emptiness. This, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is the supreme <s>yoga</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> practicing in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, which surpasses and stands above all other <s>yogas</s>. And practicing in this <s>yoga</s>, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> produces great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) and produces great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>). Practicing in this <s>yoga</s>, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not give rise to a mind of stinginess (<s>mātsarya</s>), nor a mind of
immorality (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>), nor a mind of ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>),
nor a mind of distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>), nor a mind of poor wisdom (<s>dauṣprajña</s>).
